candidates.attacker_control: Fully attacker-controlled: the `value` query parameter of the Stapler endpoint `POST /descriptorByName/com.michelin.cio.hudson.plugins.rolestrategy.RoleBasedAuthorizationStrategy/doCheckPattern?value=...`. The endpoint is `@RequirePOST` but performs no permission check, so any caller able to reach descriptor form-validation endpoints (typically any user with Overall/Read, and anonymously in configurations where anonymous has Overall/Read) can invoke it with arbitrary text. The supplied text is compiled by `Pattern.compile(value)` (line 1057) and, on a syntax error, its raw text is returned in the HTML form-validation message (line 1059).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the method is annotated @Restricted(NoExternalUse.class) (lines 1053-1054) - this is an architectural restriction only, not a permission check, and does not prevent Stapler dispatch. Verified that @RequirePOST prevents simple GET-based triggering. Verified the class's other endpoints all call checkAdminPerm() (lines 316, 374, 414, 446, 483, 506, 539, 570, 597, 775, 789, 805) and that doCheckName explicitly returns only escaped text to non-admins (lines 1076-1081), showing the author was aware of both authorization and escaping requirements elsewhere. did not find any upstream-style justification for doCheckPattern being public. No runtime testing was performed.
candidates.impact: Cross-user content/HTML injection (reflected XSS class) in the form-validation response of an administrative endpoint, reachable without the Overall/Administer privilege that the rest of the class requires; the injected markup is delivered to whichever browser renders the response. Secondary impact: an unprivileged caller can force server-side compilation of arbitrary regular expressions (resource-consumption/robustness vector) and observe regex parse-error diagnostics. Concrete impact depends on the rendering path of the response, which is not fully verifiable from this snapshot.
candidates.prerequisites: The plugin must be installed and the descriptor reachable; the caller must be able to issue an HTTP POST to the descriptor endpoint (no privileged credential is required by the code under review). To turn content injection into script execution in a victim's browser, the crafted validation request must be rendered by the victim's browser in a context that parses the response as HTML (see unverified items); CSRF crumbs and response content-type handling in the hosting Jenkins version may block simple cross-site triggering.
candidates.root_cause: `RoleBasedAuthorizationStrategy.DescriptorImpl.doCheckPattern` (RoleBasedAuthorizationStrategy.java lines 1053-1062) has no call to `checkAdminPerm()`/`Jenkins.get().checkPermission(Jenkins.ADMINISTER)`, although every other endpoint on the same descriptor (doCheckForWhitespace line 775, doAddRole line 316, doGetRole line 374, doRemoveRoles line 414, doAssignRole line 446, doDeleteSid line 483, doUnassignRole line 506, doGetAllRoles line 539, doGetMatchingJobs line 570, doGetMatchingAgents line 597, doRolesSubmit line 789, doAssignSubmit line 805) enforces Overall/Administer. In addition, the invalid-regex branch returns `FormValidation.error(pse.getMessage())` (line 1059); `java.util.regex.PatternSyntaxException.getMessage()` embeds the raw, caller-supplied pattern text plus a caret marker, and `FormValidation.error(String)` is treated as HTML by Jenkins, so the endpoint returns an HTML context containing unescaped caller-controlled characters.
candidates.title: doCheckPattern: missing permission check and unescaped attacker input in form-validation response
candidates.trace: 1) Stapler dispatches a POST to DescriptorImpl.doCheckPattern (no authorization annotation other than @RequirePOST). 2) Line 1055-1061: `value` flows directly into `Pattern.compile(value)`. 3) When compilation fails, `PatternSyntaxException.getMessage()` is passed unescaped to `FormValidation.error(...)`; the exception message contains the raw pattern text. 4) The resulting validation response is returned to the caller as an HTML-capable message. 5) Sibling validation method doCheckForWhitespace (line 774-781) explicitly gates on `checkAdminPerm()`, confirming the intended authorization model that doCheckPattern Omits.
candidates.unverified: Whether the hosting Jenkins version renders this FormValidation message via innerHTML/HTML content-type such that script executes (Jenkins versions differ; modern versions return JSON containing an HTML message fragment consumed by the UI's own JavaScript). Whether anonymous/Overall-Read callers can actually reach `/descriptorByName/...doCheckPattern` in the target deployment (core descriptor routing/permission wrappers were not inspected). Whether the CSRF crumb filter blocks a cross-site POST in the attack scenario. No exploitation or runtime confirmation was performed; this is a source-level lead only.
candidates.weakness_type: Missing authorization on HTTP form-validation endpoint plus improper neutralization of user input in output (reflected XSS/HTML injection; boundary control assumption violation)

coverage_summary: Read the complete Java main sources (RoleBasedAuthorizationStrategy, RoleMap, Role, RoleStrategyConfig, ValidationUtil, RoleBasedProjectNamingStrategy, Settings, RoleType, NamingStrategyAdministrativeMonitor, PermissionHelper, Macro, RoleMacroExtension, IMacroExtension, all three macro implementations, and all CasC classes), all webapp JavaScript, the principal resource bundles and help files, pom.xml, README/docs, and the build/CI configuration visible in scope. Established that every other mutating or admin-facing endpoint enforces Overall/Administer and @RequirePOST, which isolates doCheckPattern as the only unguarded endpoint. The relation index was used for navigation only; its 60 indexed files match the source scope (no missing files), but it does not prove reachability or data flow. Not inspected in detail: .build-config/checkstyle.xml and eclipse_formatter.xml (style only), French translation bundles, .github/dependabot.yml, release-drafter.yml, .gitignore, .mvn/extensions.xml, Messages_fr properties, MacroException/MacroExceptionCode (trivial wrappers). No tests and no Jelly views exist in this snapshot, and no build, tests, scanners, or exploits were executed.
limitations: No Jelly views are present in the snapshot, so UI rendering/escaping of role names, patterns, SIDs and Failure messages (a common XSS sink in this plugin) could not be verified; findings that depend on view templates remain unconfirmed.
No test sources are present, so intended security invariants (e.g. checks covered by Security2182Test referenced in checkstyle suppressions) could only be inferred from production code.

No runtime, build, or dynamic testing was performed; all statements about endpoint reachability (e.g. whether Overall/Read or anonymous users can invoke /descriptorByName/...doCheckPattern) and about FormValidation response content-type/rendering are unverified and depend on the hosting Jenkins core version.
The P1 relation index is navigational only (286 symbols, 839 call edges) and does not prove data flow, control flow, reachability or exploitability; no index edge was treated as a verdict.

The exact upstream commit/version is unknown (changelist is 999999-SNAPSHOT; pom suggests a 2022/2023-era baseline), so I could not diff against a known fixed revision; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: RoleMacroExtension.getMacro (src/main/java/com/synopsys/arc/jenkins/plugins/rolestrategy/RoleMacroExtension.java lines 60-72) stores null into MACRO_CACHE, a ConcurrentHashMap, on the MacroException path; ConcurrentHashMap forbids null values, so a malformed macro role name starting with '@' deterministically throws NullPointerException from inside RoleMap.hasPermission/RoleWalker during ACL evaluation, potentially breaking authorization checks instance-wide.
rejected_leads.reason: Strong code-level evidence of a latent crash bug, but the trigger (defining a role whose name begins with '@' and fails Macro.parse, e.g. '@' or '@x:bad') requires Overall/Administer through the roles configuration/API or CasC, i.e. a privileged configuration action rather than an unprivileged attacker. Classified as a robustness/DoS issue with privileged trigger, so not selected over the single strongest attacker-controlled lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Permission parsing paths in RoleBasedAuthorizationStrategy.newInstance/readRoles (lines 861 and 923) use Permission.fromId(e.getKey()) instead of PermissionHelper.resolvePermissionFromString/fromStrings, which filter out dangerous permissions (Jenkins.RUN_SCRIPTS, PluginManager.CONFIGURE_UPDATECENTER, PluginManager.UPLOAD_PLUGINS) as done in Role's DataBoundConstructor (Role.java line 99), ConverterImpl.unmarshal (line 690), RoleDefinition (line 64) and doAddRole (line 327).
rejected_leads.reason: Real inconsistency with the plugin's SECURITY-2182-style dangerous-permission suppression, and a crafted role-configuration form submission could persist roles holding dangerous permissions. However the submitting endpoint requires Overall/Administer (doRolesSubmit lines 786-797) and Role's constructor tolerates/filters null entries, so no privilege boundary is crossed relative to the submitting admin; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: DescriptorImpl.doCheckName (lines 1074-1131): `value.substring(1, value.length() - 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException/NullPointerException on short or missing values, and line 1114 returns the unescaped `v` (rather than the escaped `ev`) in a WARNING FormValidation response.
rejected_leads.reason: The unescaped branch is only reachable by a caller holding Overall/Administer because of the gate at lines 1079-1081, so any content injection is admin self-inflicted; the index-out-of-bounds is at most a request-level 500. No cross-user security impact identified.

rejected_leads.lead: RoleBasedProjectNamingStrategy.checkName(String) (lines 51-64) dereferences the result of Stapler.getCurrentRequest().findAncestorObject(ItemGroup.class) without a null check, and the 1-arg/2-arg name-convention failure message embeds the attacker-chosen item name (fullName) and admin-supplied patterns into a Failure (MessageFormat 'JobNameConventionNotApplyed', Messages.properties line 32).
rejected_leads.reason: No reachable path was established for a non-admin to cause a null ItemGroup ancestor, and the Failure text is delivered back to the requester in the item-creation error flow; the snapshot lacks the Jelly views that render Failure messages, so an XSS verdict cannot be supported from source here. Kept as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Client-side DOM construction in src/main/webapp/js/tableManage.js (lines 66, 89, 108) builds innerHTML/tooltips from the role pattern value without escaping in the input-value position (escapeHTML is applied only to the anchor text), and table.js double-escapes via escapeHTML.
rejected_leads.reason: The values originate from role patterns typed in the administrative role-management UI, so the scenario is self-XSS by an admin; the Jelly views that supply persisted patterns are not part of this snapshot, preventing verification of a stored path.

rejected_leads.lead: RoleStrategyConfig.manage page exposes role/assignment data to users granted Jenkins.SYSTEM_READ (getRequiredPermission lines 83-87) while form submissions require ADMINISTER, and doGetRole/doGetAllRoles/doGetMatchingJobs/doGetMatchingAgents return full role/SID data to Overall/Administer callers only.
rejected_leads.reason: Only admins receive the data through the Java endpoints; whether the SYSTEM_READ-gated page renders role/assignment details depends on views absent from this snapshot, so no source-supported leak could be confirmed.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins role-strategy plugin snapshot (60 model-visible files: Java main sources, webapp JS/CSS/help HTML, resource bundles/properties, pom and CI/build config; no tests and no Jelly views are present in the snapshot). The strongest source-supported defect is in the plugin's form-validation endpoint `RoleBasedAuthorizationStrategy.DescriptorImpl.doCheckPattern`: unlike every sibling `do*` endpoint in the same class (which call `checkAdminPerm()` / `checkPermission(Jenkins.ADMINISTER)`), it performs no authorization check, and it reflects the attacker-supplied `value` back in the response through `FormValidation.error(pse.getMessage())`, where `PatternSyntaxException` messages embed the raw pattern text in an HTML-accepting validation message. This is submitted as one lead, not a confirmed vulnerability. No second candidate is submitted; other leads and their counterevidence are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
